title: Agere / Adecoagro / BrasilAgro / PlayAGS / AGTC / Agrium / Arctic Glacier / Agribrands — Cash Quality, FCF Conversion and Event Timing V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: Adecoagro 2015, BrasilAgro 2007, PlayAGS 2019, Agrium 2002, Arctic Glacier 2014, Arctic Glacier 2019 and Agribrands 2000.
AGX 2000 is Agribrands International, not Argan Inc.; the SQL company mapping reflects historical ticker reuse.
Source SQL performance rows are available only for Adecoagro 2015 and 2019.
Agere 2002 return requires the 2005 1-for-10 reverse split and the 2007 fixed 2.16-LSI-share merger exchange ratio.
Adecoagro 2015 nearly met its 2016 EBITDA forecast but badly missed the thesis FCF bridge; Adecoagro 2019 nearly met its 2021 EBITDA plan and subsequently formalized capital returns.
BrasilAgro's early farmland sales strongly validated asset-level economics, but the listed stock was hit by the 2008 market collapse.
PlayAGS was acquired in 2025 for $12.50 cash/share, below the inferred 2019 VIC entry around $18.6.
AGTC was acquired for $0.34 upfront plus a CVR of up to $0.73; the CVR maximum is not treated as realized value.
Agrium exceeded the author's ~$4 peak EPS forecast with $4.89 diluted EPS in 2005, but the $35-$40 stock target arrived later in the cycle.
Arctic Glacier 2014 and 2019 are liquidation/residual-cash trust-unit ideas. Exact USD IRRs are not forced because distributions span USD and CAD across multiple years.
The Arctic Glacier November 2019 distribution had already gone ex before the November 18, 2019 VIC post and therefore is excluded from the post-entry payoff.
Agribrands received a superior Cargill bid of $54.50 cash/share in December 2000, replacing the Ralcorp transaction.

batch_lessons: A visible balance-sheet asset is not automatically shareholder value: cash quality depends on future burn, commitments and timing.
EBITDA forecasts and free-cash-flow forecasts must be treated as separate hypotheses.
Already-deployed growth capex is generally easier to validate than policy-driven macro optionality.
Realized farm-sale IRRs can be excellent while listed equity performs poorly because market beta and timing are separate variables.
M&A optionality must be evaluated using the actual takeout price, not the mere occurrence of an acquisition.
Clinical-biotech cash is runway rather than excess cash and should be reduced by future trial burn and financing friction.
Commodity earnings peaks and equity multiple peaks often arrive at different times.
Liquidation investments require dated cash-flow modeling; nominal recovery can coexist with a poor IRR.
Ex-distribution dates determine entitlement and can completely change an apparent residual-cash arbitrage.
Historical ticker reuse can silently map a successful old idea to the wrong modern company; legal-entity verification is mandatory.
